newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Analysts see Czech petrochem stocks undervalued.
newsitem.headline: Analysts see Czech petrochem stocks undervalued.

text.p: Shares in Czech petrochemical companies Kaucuk Group a.s. and Chemopetrol Group a.s. are undervalued, analysts say, despite uncertainty about their future financial results.
On Tuesday, Chemopetrol closed up 33 crowns on the Prague Stock Exchange (PSE) to 1,133 putting the issue 7.3 percent higher than one month ago.
Kaucuk closed three crowns lower to 1,100, five percent above its price of one month ago.
Analysts polled by Reuters said that both companies were attractive investments at up to 1,200 crowns per share.

"Shares in Chemopetrol Group and Kaucuk Group are currently attractive buys both from a price earnings point of view and in view of the ratio of market capitalisation and total revenues," said Jan Zak of Atlantik Financni Trhy.
Nevertheless, Zak added, Kaucuk this year and Chemopetrol next year are likely to post lower profits.
"Compared with 1995 we expect a fall in Kaucuk's net profit of 30.6 percent to 500 million crowns." Zak said the decline in profits was partly caused by provisioning for bad debts.

Although Chemopetrol's 1996 profits are forecast to rise to around 900 million crowns, this was caused partly because Chemopetrol heavily provisioned against its own debts in 1995, thereby lowering the base against which comparisons are made.
The performance of Kaucuk and Chempetrol takes place against the background of radical changes during the privatisation of the Czech petrochemical industry.
At the end of 1995 both companies divested their refineries into a government-created company Ceska Rafinerska a.s.

The move was part of a long term plan which should culminate next year in a 100 percent swap of Chemopetrol and Kaucuk shares for shares in Unipetrol a.s. which is a holding company with a 51 percent stake in Ceska Rafinerska.
The IOC consortium of Du Pont de Nemours unit Conoco, Royal Dutch/Shell and Italy's Agip won a 49 percent stake in Ceska Rafinerska last year.

In November, the boards of Chemopetrol, Kaucuk and Unipetrol said they had agreed to swap one Chemopetrol share for between 1.05 to 1.20 Unipetrol shares, and one Kaucuk share for between 1.10 to 1.25 Unipetrol shares.
Analysts said that because the potential ranges for the share still overlap, arbitrage prospects ahead of the swap were not clear.
Final approval of the swap ratio must come from extraordinary meetings of each companies' shareholders, probably in the first quarter of next year.
Chemopetrol said on Tuesday that a recent fire at its primary supplier, the Litvinov oil refinery owned by Ceska Rafinerska a.s., will not hurt 1996 profits.

Financial director Otakar Wolf said the mid-November fire at Rafinerska's neighbouring tank station near the northern city of Litvinov halted raw materials supplies to Chemopetrol and caused a 40 percent decrease of production for one week.
